note: Set B captures two important facts that A omits: that both controllers use the generator speed measurement as the sole feedback input, and that no control actions were developed to regulate the nacelle-yaw angle. Set A instead repeats the nonpower-production claim under two different entity names and adds a near-trivial 'conventional design approach' claim. Both sets bind the two-control-system and filter-type claims correctly and share the same mild over-attribution of the generic 'such wind turbines' control architecture to the NREL 5-MW turbine. B is somewhat more repetitive (three duplicated fact pairs vs. A's two), but its coverage of substantive facts is clearly better.
remarks: Both sets state the filter-type fact twice with only differing condition wording, and B additionally splits the sole-feedback-input fact into four claims (per controller x per condition). Neither set extracts the filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) or the definitions of alpha, n, Ts, fc, which are the main quantitative content of Section 7.1.
